attempts.approach: Follows the source proof directly. (1) `exists_int_of_cos_nonneg`: the inverse image of {cos ≥ 0} is the union of intervals [−π/2 + 2πk, π/2 + 2πk]; proved by taking k = round(x/(2π)), so y = x − 2πk ∈ [−π, π] (via `abs_sub_round`), cos y = cos x ≥ 0 (`Real.cos_sub_int_mul_two_pi`), and excluding y ∈ (π/2, π] and y ∈ [−π, −π/2) with `Real.cos_neg_of_pi_div_two_lt_of_lt` (+ `Real.cos_neg`). (2) `int_eq_of_step_lt_pi`: consecutive such intervals are separated by a gap of length π, so a step with |y − x| < π cannot change the integer label k (case split on `lt_trichotomy`, `Int.add_one_le_iff`, linarith). (3) `transport_angle_interval_of_cos`: `choose` the label k i for each θ i − α, show by `Fin.induction` using the step hypothesis that k i = k 0 for all i, and take c = α − π/2 + 2π k 0. (4) Converse: α = c + π/2 gives θ i − α ∈ [−π/2, π/2], so `Real.cos_nonneg_of_neg_pi_div_two_le_of_le`. (5) Bridge between the plane-vector formulation and the angular one: `planeDot (unitDir α) (unitDir θ) = cos (θ − α)` (via `Real.cos_sub`), and every unit vector v (planeDot v v = 1) equals unitDir (Complex.arg (planeComplex v)) using the library's `planeComplex`, `euclideanLength_formula`, and Mathlib's `Complex.cos_arg` / `Complex.sin_arg`. Compiles in ~6 s via `lake env lean ../drafts/AngleInterval.lean` with no warnings or errors; imports SM.EuclideanPlane plus Mathlib Trigonometric.Basic, Complex.Arg, Algebra.Order.Round.

attempts.fidelity_notes: Source (sm-5-transport.tex lines 133–148): 'If a finite real sequence θ_0,…,θ_N has |θ_{i+1}−θ_i|<π, and all its unit directions lie in a closed semicircle, then all its real entries lie in one interval of length π. Conversely, containment of all entries in such an interval puts their unit directions in a closed semicircle.' Encoding choices: (a) the sequence is `θ : Fin (N+1) → ℝ` (so N ≥ 0 and there are N+1 entries θ_0..θ_N), steps are `∀ i : Fin N, |θ i.succ − θ i.castSucc| < π`, exactly |θ_{i+1} − θ_i| < π for 0 ≤ i < N; (b) 'unit directions' are `unitDir (θ i) = (Real.cos (θ i), Real.sin (θ i)) : Plane` with the library's `Plane = ℝ × ℝ`; (c) 'lie in a closed semicircle' is `InClosedSemicircle θ`: ∃ unit vector v (`planeDot v v = 1`, the Euclidean unit-norm condition in coordinates) with `0 ≤ planeDot v (unitDir (θ i))` for all i — i.e. all directions lie in the closed half-plane {⟨v,·⟩ ≥ 0}, whose intersection with the unit circle is exactly a closed semicircle; the equivalent angular form ∃ α, ∀ i, 0 ≤ cos (θ i − α) is proved as `inClosedSemicircle_iff` and both forms of the theorem are provided; (d) 'lie in one interval of length π' is `∃ c, ∀ i, c ≤ θ i ∧ θ i ≤ c + π` (closed interval [c, c+π]; the source's proof explicitly uses the closed intervals [α+2πk, α+π+2πk]). The converse is stated for an arbitrary index type ι and without the step hypothesis, which is strictly more general than the source's statement (the source does not need the step hypothesis for the converse either); `transport_angle_interval_iff` packages both directions under the source's hypotheses. No SM geometry (chirotopes, rot, μ_i, ℓ_i) enters: the lemma is pure real analysis and is stated as such, exactly as in the source.

attempts.approach: Checked with `cd work/lean && lake env lean ../drafts/StarPolygons.lean` (706 lines, imports SM.PositiveRotationSeed and SM.ShiftTheorem; zero errors, zero warnings). Structure: (1) `unitPoint N k = (cos(2πk/N), sin(2πk/N))` via k.val; `unitPoint_intCast` (any integer representative gives the same point, using ZMod.val_intCast + Int.emod_add_ediv_mul + Real.cos/sin_add_int_mul_two_pi); `unitPoint_injective` via Real.Angle.cos_sin_inj, angle_eq_iff_two_pi_dvd_sub and Int.eq_zero_of_abs_lt_dvd; `rotationMap_unitPoint`: R_{2πm/N} u_k = u_{k+m} by the addition formulas. (2) Relation to the accepted seed: `positiveRotationSeed_eq_unitPoint` (seed vertex j = u_{rj}, through Complex.exp_nat_mul and exp_ofReal_mul_I_re/im), hence `star r = shift (-1) (positiveRotationSeed r)` and `shift 1 (star r) = positiveRotationSeed r`; Regular, principalTurn = 2πr/N and rotationNumber = r are transported with regular_shift_forward, principalTurn_shift, rotationNumber_shift, cyclicComplexSeed_principalTurn, positiveSeedRatio_arg, positiveRotationSeed_rotation; turn = 1 from turn_det + principalAngle_sign. (3) gcd(r,2r+1)=1 by divisibility of (2r+1)-2r; r is a unit mod N (ZMod.isUnit_iff_coprime), giving `star_injective`. (4) Geometry (ii) from three algebraic facts: |μ_t|² = 1, μ_{t+1} = R μ_t (so ⟨μ_t,μ_{t+1}⟩ = cos θ, det(μ_t,μ_{t+1}) = sin θ), whence ⟨m_t, ℓ_t⟩ = 0, |m_t|² = (1+cos θ)/2 = cos²(πr/N) (Real.cos_sq), |x(t)|² = ρ² + (t-1/2)²|ℓ_t|² (tangency, equality only at the midpoint since |ℓ_t|² = 2-2cos θ > 0), det(ℓ_t, 0-μ_t) = sin θ > 0. (5) Genericity: `circle_three_points` (three distinct points with equal |·|² are never collinear, via scalar_of_det_zero and λ(λ-1)|b-a|² = 0) gives G1 with distinctness from `star_injective`. G2: every point of edge line t satisfies ⟨x, m_t⟩ = ρ²; midpoints are pairwise distinct (`star_midpoint_injective`: coinciding midpoints would put μ_s, μ_{s+1} on the chord line of edge t, forcing s ∈ {t,t+1} and s+1 ∈ {t,t+1}, impossible since 1 ≠ 0 ≠ 2 in ZMod (2r+1)); a common interior point x ≠ 0 of three edges is orthogonal to m_j - m_i and m_k - m_i, so det(m_j-m_i, m_k-m_i) = 0, contradicting `circle_three_points` on the ρ-circle (this is the 'at most two tangents through a point' argument in algebraic form). (6) K_{-r} = reversal (star r): Generic via generic_reversal, turns -1 via turn_reversal, rotationNumber -r via rotationNumber_reversal, principal turns -θ via principalTurn_reversal. Bundled as `star_generic_lemma`.

attempts.approach: Follows the source proof. (1) Pointwise: the 'no closed half-plane' hypothesis gives, by compactness of the Euclidean unit circle {planeDot v v = 1} (closed + bounded in ℝ×ℝ) and a maximum of v ↦ ∑ min 0 ⟨v, w i⟩, a uniform gap δ > 0 with ∀ unit v ∃ i, ⟨v, w i⟩ ≤ -δ. The set K of convex combinations (image of stdSimplex, compact and convex via Mathlib) contains x = -ε b for b = ∑ w i and ε = δ/(|b|+1): otherwise the nearest point p of K to x gives q = p - x ≠ 0 with ⟨q, w i⟩ ≥ |q|² - ε⟨q,b⟩ for all i (variational inequality proved from minimality along the segment p + s(y-p) with an explicit s), which contradicts the gap via Cauchy–Schwarz (|q|² - ε|q||b| ≤ -δ|q| ⇒ |q| ≤ ε|b| - δ < 0). Then l i = a i + ε is strictly positive and closing (transport:positive-close). (2) Local: pick p, q with det(u p t₀, u q t₀) ≠ 0 (exists, otherwise the perpendicular of a nonzero member is a closed-half-plane witness), correct the two coordinates by the Cramer formulas transport:cramer; continuity on {D ≠ 0}, vanishing at t₀, so a neighbourhood {D ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ i, 0 < l i t} ∈ 𝓝 t₀ exists (Filter.eventually_all). (3) Global: extend u continuously from Icc a b to ℝ by projIcc (so the hypothesis holds at every real t), take a finite subcover of the compact Icc a b by interiors of the local neighbourhoods (IsCompact.elim_nhds_subcover), a continuous partition of unity subordinate to it (PartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate on ℝ, s = Icc a b), multiply each weight by the local lengths extended by zero via Set.indicator (continuous because tsupport ⊆ U j), and sum: positivity since some weight is positive at each t ∈ s and all terms are ≥ 0; closing by linearity (Finset.sum_comm). (4) Endpoint join: the set of positive closing vectors at fixed directions is convex (convex_positiveClosing); the segment (1-s) m + s l(a) resp. l(b) is the explicit join.

The compact interval is Set.Icc a b with a ≤ b (a = b allowed, matching the source's one-point case).
